text:
A few private companies now offer short trips beyond the atmosphere to those who can pay, and some people believe that space tourism will benefit humanity. Others disagree. This essay will consider both perspectives before explaining my own opinion.

On the one hand, supporters argue that space tourism may drive new technology and inspire people. Competition between companies can lower the cost of rockets, and developments in materials, engines and life-support systems often find uses on Earth, as earlier space programmes did. The sight of ordinary people travelling to orbit may also encourage young people to study science and engineering, and astronauts who see the planet from space often describe a stronger sense of its fragility and unity. A company that learns to reuse rockets, for example, may make future satellite launches cheaper, which benefits communication and weather forecasting. Over time, space tourism might even help to develop research facilities in orbit.

On the other hand, critics point out that its benefits to humanity are uncertain. Flights are affordable only to the very rich, release significant emissions and carry real risks, and the same money and talent could be used on problems such as poverty, disease and climate change. Public attention and funding may also be diverted from more useful space science, such as monitoring the Earth. A flight that costs as much as a hospital ward, for instance, seems a poor use of resources when many people lack basic care. Supporters of the industry may exaggerate its social value to attract investors.

In conclusion, both views have merit. Personally, I believe that space tourism is mainly an entertainment for the wealthy, and that its benefits to humanity will be limited unless emissions are controlled and the technology serves wider scientific goals.

plan.think: Mở bài mô tả hiện trạng (vài công ty tư nhân bán chuyến ngắn ra ngoài khí quyển); mỗi thân bài một phía; ý kiến riêng thiên về hoài nghi có điều kiện.

Cạnh tranh giảm chi phí tên lửa; vật liệu, động cơ, hệ thống hỗ trợ sự sống có ứng dụng trên Trái Đất; truyền cảm hứng người trẻ học khoa học; phi hành gia thấy hành tinh mong manh. Ví dụ công ty học tái sử dụng tên lửa làm phóng vệ tinh rẻ hơn.

Chỉ người rất giàu mua nổi, phát thải đáng kể, rủi ro; tiền và nhân tài có thể dùng cho nghèo đói, bệnh tật, khí hậu; sự chú ý có thể chệch khỏi khoa học vũ trụ hữu ích hơn. Ví dụ chuyến bay đắt bằng một khoa bệnh viện.
Chủ yếu là giải trí cho người giàu; lợi ích hạn chế trừ khi kiểm soát phát thải và phục vụ mục tiêu khoa học rộng hơn.
